source_text: XI. Ταῦτα εἴποντος αὐτοῦ μόλις ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου ἐσφιγμένους ὥστε συμπνίγεσθαι ἐνέβαλον αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν φυλακὴν παραδόντες τοῖς δεσμοφύλαξιν. Εἰσελθόντες δὲ εὗρον κατακεκλεισμένον πρεσβύτερον τῆς καθολικῆς ἐκκλησίας ὀνόματι Λίμνον καὶ γυναῖκα Μακεδονίαν ἀπὸ κώμης Καρίνης καὶ ἕνα ἐκ τῆς αἱρέσεως τῶν Φρυγῶν ὀνόματι Εὐτυχιανόν. Ὄντων οὖν αὐτῶν κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ ἔγνωσαν οἱ ἐπὶ τῆς φυλακῆς ὅτι τὰ φερόμενα ὑπὸ τῶν πιστῶν οὐ λαμβάνουσιν οἱ περὶ τὸν Πιόνιον. Ἔλεγε γὰρ ὁ Πιόνιος ὅτι· Ὅτε πλειόνων ἐχρῄζομεν οὐδένα ἐβαρήσαμεν, καὶ νῦν πῶς ληψόμεθα;
pass_a_gloss: With him having said these things, with difficulty, having been squeezed out of the crowd so as to be choked, they threw them into the prison, handing them over to the jailers. And having gone in they found a shut-up elder of the catholic church by name Limnos and a woman Macedonia from the village of Karina and one out of the heresy of the Phrygians by name Eutychianos. While they were together in the same place, those in charge of the prison came to know that those around Pionius are not accepting the things being brought by the believers. For Pionius was saying that: When we needed more things we burdened no one, and now how shall we take?
pass_b_english: When he had spoken these words, they were barely forced through the pressing crowd, packed so tight they could hardly breathe, and then they were cast into the prison and handed over to the jailers. Once inside, they found there a confined elder of the catholic church named Linus, and a woman named Macedonia from the village of Karina, and one man from the sect of the Phrygians named Eutychian.

While they were all together in the same place, the keepers of the prison learned that Pionius and those with him were refusing what the believers kept bringing. For Pionius kept saying, When we were in greater need we burdened no one, so how should we accept anything now?
